description: THE HOLE: the committed read-only ClusterRole grants get/list/watch on resources: ["*"] — that wildcard is what makes Secrets readable, and it was left in deliberately for this beat
command: R=platform/rbac/agent-readonly.yaml; [ -f "$R" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'resources: \["\*"\]' "$R" && echo wildcard || echo scoped

description: THE HOLE, MEASURED: under the committed read-only kubeconfig, 'get secrets' succeeds — the agent's own identity can read every Secret in the namespace, not just workload state
command: KC=platform/kubeconfigs/agent-readonly.yaml; [ -f "$KC" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; kubectl --kubeconfig="$KC" auth can-i get secrets -n northstar 2>/dev/null || echo no

description: YOUR FIX: platform/rbac/agent-readonly-tightened.yaml exists — the learner closes the hole by authoring a scoped ClusterRole, not by editing the live cluster by hand
YOUR FIX: the tightened role names an explicit resource list, not resources: ["*"] — a wildcard resource grant cannot be narrowed by omission, it has to be replaced
command: R=platform/rbac/agent-readonly-tightened.yaml; [ -f "$R" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'resources: \["\*"\]' "$R" && echo still-wildcard || echo explicit-list

description: YOUR FIX: the tightened role's resource list never names secrets — the one resource the triage skill never needs to read
command: R=platform/rbac/agent-readonly-tightened.yaml; [ -f "$R" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -q 'secrets' "$R" && echo still-includes-secrets || echo excludes-secrets

description: YOUR FIX: the tightened role still names pods, deployments and configmaps — closing the Secrets hole must not silently break the triage skill's own evidence reads
command: R=platform/rbac/agent-readonly-tightened.yaml; [ -f "$R" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; for r in pods deployments configmaps; do grep -q "$r" "$R" || { echo broke-core-reads; exit 0; }; done; echo core-reads-intact

description: YOUR FIX: the tightened role still grants only get/list/watch — narrowing the resource list is not an excuse to also add a write verb
command: R=platform/rbac/agent-readonly-tightened.yaml; [ -f "$R" ] || { echo missing; exit 0; }; grep -Eq '"(create|update|patch|delete)"' "$R" && echo write-verb-present || echo read-only
